correctness.rationale: For the two-mode SPD quadratic with κ>1 and r=v²/u²>0, compute F_j=(g_{j,1}²+g_{j,2}²/κ)/2. The Cauchy step multiplies g_0 modes by (κ−1)r/(1+κr) and −(κ−1)/(1+κr). Its secant is parallel to g_0, so the second step a has a²=(1+r)/(1+κ²r), in (1/κ²,1), and multiplies the modes by 1−a,1−κa. Substitution gives the displayed ratio. Bounding the two squared factors by 1 and κ²a² respectively and using κ²r a²<1+r bounds the ratio by κ²(κr²+1+r)/[(1+κr)²(κ+r)]. The denominator less κ(κr²+1+r) is r(2κ²−κ+1)+r²(κ³−κ²+2κ)+κ²r³>0. Nonnegativity follows from the squared energy. For r=κ^(−3/2) the first energy ratio is asymptotic to κ^(−1/2), a is asymptotic to κ^(−1/4), and the next ratio is asymptotic to κ^(3/2), squeezing the rescaled supremum to one. Exact replay using g_0=(sqrt(63),1), κ=9 gives step lengths 8/9,2/3 and energies 284/9,28/9,5516/81, hence all three rational ratios. The argument proves neither a finite-κ optimizer nor later-step control; absent-mode or stationary seeds are excluded as stated. The text output is recorded evidence only, distinct from the independent mode and rational-energy calculations.

value.rationale: A practitioner using the natural exact-search warm-up and established curvature rule cannot infer net progress from first-step decrease or asymptotic convergence. The sharp initial-to-final coefficient quantifies how much progress can be lost and identifies an adverse scale for the starting spectral mixture, going beyond an example of overshoot or a loose previous-iterate bound. The result is deliberately only about two exact updates on the stated two-mode model.
